title: Series circuits
target: Use current continuity and voltage drops in a single-path circuit.
criteria: Check that voltage drops add to the supply voltage.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A battery, switch, and two resistors form one loop with no branches. Which statement is correct for steady current?
options: Each resistor must have the same voltage.
Both resistors carry the same current.
The second resistor always carries zero current.
cpa.guide: One path requires the same steady charge flow through each component; voltage drops can differ.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: One connection in a simple two-resistor series loop opens. What happens after transients settle?
options: The other resistor doubles its current.
The open gap has zero voltage in every case.
Only the second resistor loses current.
cpa.guide: Opening the only path stops steady loop current.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: Resistors of 7 Ω and 11 Ω are in series. What is equivalent resistance?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: An ideal 20 V source supplies series resistors of 4 Ω and 6 Ω. What current passes through the 6 Ω resistor?
cpa.guide: Equivalent resistance is 10 Ω. Loop current is 20/10 = 2 A through both.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: In a 14 V series loop, two component drops are 5 V and 3 V. What is the third drop with ideal wires?
cpa.guide: The drops sum to supply voltage: 14 − 5 − 3 = 6 V.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A student reports 2 A through series resistors of 3 Ω and 8 Ω powered by 22 V. Which check confirms consistency?
options: The currents must add to 4 A at the battery.
Drops are 6 V and 16 V, totaling 22 V.
Drops are 3 V and 8 V, totaling 11 V.
cpa.guide: V = IR gives 6 and 16 V; the same current passes through both.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.
